values.value: Before you start, one thing about how we will read your answers. The two ends of this move are not equally known. Nothing reads HubSpot — there is no source connector, so every count you give us is your description of the estate rather than a measurement of it. The destination is the opposite: Marketing Cloud Engagement has a real capability manifest, a target adapter that scaffolds against it, and live tenant access. So we treat the estate figures as illustrative and the named gaps as not: they are structural properties of Journey Builder, Content Builder and Data Extensions, and they will be true of your estate whatever its size turns out to be.

[{"pattern":"smart_list_continuous_reevaluation","status":"partial","severity":"major","category":"audience","issue":"Automation depends on active (smart) list membership that is continuously re-evaluated, including automatic removal","gloss":"HubSpot active lists are live \u2014 contacts join AND LEAVE as criteria stop matching. Marketing Cloud cannot evaluate filter membership at runtime, so an active list becomes a scheduled Automation Studio query and membership is stale between runs.","workaround":"Convert each active list to a scheduled-refresh audience and set the refresh cadence from the automation's real sensitivity rather than from a default. Where membership is read inside a decision, pre-calculate it as a boolean on the entry Data Extension. Where automatic REMOVAL is load-bearing \u2014 suppression lists above all \u2014 implement the removal explicitly: a stale suppression list mails people who opted out.","manual_steps":["Inventory active lists and the workflows that consume them","For each, establish how fast membership changes must propagate \u2014 in minutes, hours or days","Set a refresh cadence per audience from that answer, and write it down as a commitment","Add a boolean per list to the entry DE where a decision reads membership, populated by a Query Activity before entry","Identify every list whose REMOVAL behaviour matters and implement removal explicitly","Audit suppression-role lists first \u2014 those are the compliance-relevant ones"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"crm_lives_inside_hubspot","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"data_model","issue":"Marketing automation reads and writes CRM records that live in HubSpot's own CRM, not in an external system of record","gloss":"In an Eloqua or SFMC estate the CRM is somewhere else and the marketing platform syncs to it. In HubSpot the CRM IS the platform, so a marketing migration has to answer a question that never arises otherwise: where does the CRM go?","workaround":"This is a scoping decision, not a technical workaround. Three outcomes, with completely different cost and cutover risk: HubSpot stays as the CRM and Marketing Cloud integrates to it via Marketing Cloud Connect; the CRM moves to Sales Cloud; or the estate splits, marketing on Salesforce and sales still in HubSpot. Force it to the surface in Assess and get it decided before Blueprint.","manual_steps":["Inventory which CRM objects marketing automation actually reads and writes","Establish whether Sales and Service will remain on HubSpot post-migration","Decide: HubSpot stays as CRM / CRM moves to Sales Cloud / the estate splits","If HubSpot stays, design the integration and name its owner and its budget","If the CRM moves, add a CRM migration workstream \u2014 it is not in the marketing scope"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"workflow_loop_go_to_action","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"flow_control","issue":"Source workflow uses a go-to-action step that jumps backwards, forming a loop","gloss":"Journey Builder is strictly forward-only \u2014 contacts never move backwards. Typical HubSpot loops are poll-until-qualified, retry-N-times and hold-until-eligible.","workaround":"Classify each backward edge, then convert it. Poll-until-true becomes Wait By Attribute on a pre-calculated datetime. Retry-N-times becomes an unrolled fixed-count sequence, and the truncation gets documented. Hold-until-eligible is not a loop at all \u2014 it routes to the frequency- capping infrastructure. Where nothing fits, split into multiple journeys chained by Fire Event.","manual_steps":["Trace every go-to-action edge and mark the ones that point backwards","Classify each backward edge: poll / retry / hold","For poll: pre-calculate the exit datetime or boolean into the entry DE","For retry: unroll to a fixed maximum count and document the truncation","For hold: route to the frequency-capping suppression DE instead","Where nothing else fits, split into multiple journeys connected by Fire Event"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"workflow_reenrollment","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"flow_control","issue":"Source workflow has re-enrolment enabled \u2014 records re-enter on repeat trigger matches","gloss":"Journey Builder has no re-enrolment concept. Entry is per-injection, so the source of repeated entry is rebuilt outside the journey as a scheduled query.","workaround":"Enable re-entry on the target journey, then build a scheduled Automation Studio query that injects re-qualifying contacts, plus a last-entered-date attribute the injection guards against so nobody enters twice inside the intended window. Validate the cadence against the source's REAL re-enrolment frequency, not against its configuration.","manual_steps":["Record each workflow's re-enrolment triggers and its observed re-enrolment frequency","Enable re-entry on the target journey","Build a scheduled Automation Studio query that injects re-qualifiers","Add a last-entered-date attribute and guard the injection against it","Validate re-entry cadence against the source's real behaviour"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"workflow_goal_criteria","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"flow_control","issue":"Source workflow declares goal criteria that both auto-unenrol records and define the conversion metric","gloss":"A HubSpot goal does two jobs \u2014 it exits the record on conversion and it supplies the workflow's headline conversion rate. Journey Builder provides the first as Exit Criteria and the second not at all.","workaround":"Split the goal in two. The exit half becomes journey Exit Criteria, and its evaluation frequency has to be confirmed rather than assumed \u2014 HubSpot's is near-continuous. The metric half is a reporting requirement handed to whoever owns reporting; it does not travel with the journey. Flag any workflow whose goal is its only success measure, because that report otherwise disappears silently.","manual_steps":["Extract the goal filter for every workflow that has one","Implement the exit half as journey Exit Criteria","Confirm the target's evaluation frequency against HubSpot's near-continuous one","Hand the conversion-metric definition to the reporting workstream explicitly","Flag any workflow whose goal is its ONLY success measure"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"hubdb_dependency","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"data_model","issue":"CONDITIONAL ON SCOPE \u2014 where HubDB-backed content is expected to move, that content depends on tables queried at render time","gloss":"HubDB is a relational store HubL queries WHILE RENDERING, and most of what it backs is HubSpot CMS \u2014 landing pages, site pages, blog listings. Whether any of that is in this migration is the cms_scope_expectation probe, not an assumption this callout gets to make. Where the answer is that it stays on HubSpot CMS, this is a boundary to write down and nothing more. Where the answer is that it moves, or where an EMAIL renders from a HubDB query, it is a blocker: nothing in Marketing Cloud renders from an arbitrary queried table at send time, so the data moves to a Data Extension and the render-time query becomes an AMPscript Lookup or a pre-computed value.","workaround":"Settle the scope question first \u2014 read the cms_scope_expectation answer before pricing any of this. If HubSpot CMS is being kept, record the boundary, confirm nothing in the EMAIL estate queries HubDB, and stop here. If the content is expected to move, or an email does query a table, split it into a data problem and a rendering problem. Each HubDB table becomes a Data Extension. Each render-time query becomes either an AMPscript Lookup, for a static lookup, or a value pre-computed into the send audience where it is dynamic per recipient. Listing-style content \u2014 a variable-length list rendered from a table \u2014 is the case that does not convert; rebuild it as a dynamic block or accept reduced fidelity.","manual_steps":["Read the cms_scope_expectation answer first: is HubSpot CMS being kept, moved, or moved as a separate programme?","Confirm separately whether any MARKETING EMAIL renders from a HubDB query \u2014 that half is in scope whatever happens to the website","If the content stays on HubSpot CMS, write the boundary into the scope document and stop","Inventory HubDB tables and every HubL query against them","Classify each query: static lookup / per-recipient dynamic / listing","Model each table as a Data Extension","Replace static lookups with AMPscript Lookup or a merge field","Pre-compute per-recipient dynamic values into the entry audience","Rebuild listing-style content as a dynamic block, or accept reduced fidelity"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"hubl_templating","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"personalization","issue":"Email, template, or module contains HubL beyond simple token substitution","gloss":"HubL is a full templating language. Plain tokens port to merge fields trivially; loops, conditionals, macros, filters, includes and HubDB or CRM queries do not. Against classic Marketing Cloud this is a rewrite into AMPscript, not a redesign.","workaround":"Classify every HubL construct before estimating, and estimate by construct count rather than by email count. Plain token becomes a merge field, mechanically. Conditional or loop over the contact's own attributes becomes a dynamic content block. A HubDB or CRM-object query needs the data pre-joined first. Macro, include and filter chains are rebuilt as a target-native block. Render-diff the top-volume emails against production samples rather than trusting the rewrite.","manual_steps":["Pull template and module source via the CMS API and inventory HubL constructs","Classify each construct: token / attribute conditional / data query / macro chain","Rebuild in Content Builder, using AMPscript where the construct needs logic","Render-diff the output against production samples for the top-volume emails"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"custom_modules","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"personalization","issue":"Content is assembled from custom modules \u2014 parameterised HubL components with typed fields","gloss":"A mature HubSpot content system is a module library, not a set of emails. Content Builder has content blocks and template slots, which recover part of the reuse but not the typed-field component model, so the abstraction flattens unless a target-side library is built first.","workaround":"Do not port module by module. Inventory modules by USAGE COUNT, build a small library of content blocks and templates covering the high-usage ones, and inline the long tail with a record of what was dropped. Budget the library build as its own task BEFORE content migration starts, and warn the client that the editor's workflow changes \u2014 that is a change-management item, not a build item.","manual_steps":["Export module source and field definitions via the CMS API","Rank modules by usage count across emails and email templates; rank site usage separately and only if cms_scope_expectation says the web estate is moving","Design a Content Builder block and template library covering the top modules","Inline or retire the long tail, and record what was dropped","Brief the content team on the editing-experience change before cutover"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"forms_and_ctas_rebuild","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"content","issue":"HubSpot forms and CTAs are embedded across customer-owned web properties","gloss":"Forms and CTAs are embed scripts served from HubSpot and dropped into pages marketing may not own. Target-side they become CloudPages plus Web Collect, and every swap is a website release on somebody else's schedule.","workaround":"Run the site form scan FIRST \u2014 it is the one HubSpot capability the accelerator already has, and it finds embeds on customer-owned domains that no tenant export will ever show you. Reconcile what it finds against the in-tenant form inventory; the delta is the real risk. Then disposition each embed: port to a CloudPage with Web Collect, bridge it (keep the HubSpot form posting and relay submissions), rebuild, or retire. Bridging is often the only way to avoid a big-bang website change.","manual_steps":["Run a site form scan across all customer-owned domains before scoping forms","Reconcile discovered embeds against the in-tenant form inventory","Identify who owns each hosting web property and whether they have capacity","Disposition each form and CTA: port / bridge / rebuild / retire","Inventory legacy versus new-editor CTAs separately and state what happens to each one's analytics history","Plan the embed swap as a website release, on the web team's schedule, not marketing's"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"lead_scoring_model_no_export","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"scoring","issue":"Estate uses HubSpot lead scoring; predictive scores in particular have no exportable model","gloss":"Rule-based scoring is readable and can be transcribed. Predictive scoring is not exportable at all \u2014 only current values come out, and classic Marketing Cloud has no native scoring engine to receive either, so scoring lands in a query, an automation, or upstream in the CRM.","workaround":"Transcribe rule-based scoring and rebuild it target-side, accepting that decay and time-frame criteria may need explicit date attributes. Migrate predictive values as a dated, frozen snapshot for continuity, declare an explicit end-of-life for that snapshot, and plan the replacement model as a post-migration workstream with its own budget. Warn Sales explicitly: score-driven routing degrading is a sales-visible failure.","manual_steps":["Transcribe every scoring rule set before tenant access ends","Identify which downstream automation and routing depends on score thresholds","Decide where scoring will live \u2014 Automation Studio query, or upstream in the CRM","Rebuild rule-based scoring and reconcile against a sample cohort","Export current predictive values as a dated snapshot and agree its expiry","Name the owner of the replacement model, and brief Sales"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"sequences_out_of_scope","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"scope","issue":"Estate uses HubSpot Sequences \u2014 a Sales Hub capability outside the marketing migration's scope and budget","gloss":"Sequences are rep-sent 1:1 cadences from a connected mailbox, licensed under Sales Hub and owned by Sales. The Salesforce counterpart is Sales Engagement \u2014 a different product, a different budget line, usually a different buyer.","workaround":"Decide explicitly whether Sequences are in or out, in Assess rather than Execute. If in, they route to the Sales Cloud workstream rather than being absorbed here. If out, get it written down, and confirm what happens to them at HubSpot decommissioning \u2014 that is a hard dependency on the CRM decision above.","manual_steps":["Ask Sales \u2014 not Marketing \u2014 whether Sequences are in use and how heavily","Establish the licence and budget owner","Record an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope decision in the engagement scope document","If out of scope, confirm what happens at HubSpot decommissioning"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"reporting_no_port_path","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"reporting","issue":"Saved reports, dashboards, and attribution reports have no export path and no target equivalent","gloss":"HubSpot's report builder spans marketing AND CRM objects in one query surface because they are one database. There is no API for report definitions, and classic Marketing Cloud's native reporting is materially weaker \u2014 so this is the gap most likely to be found after go-live, by an executive whose dashboard is empty.","workaround":"Treat reporting as a parallel workstream from day one rather than a migration deliverable. Inventory the reports actually VIEWED \u2014 usually far fewer than the number that exist \u2014 rebuild those, and get written acceptance that pre-cutover attribution history does not come along. Retain a read-only HubSpot seat past cutover if historic reporting must stay reachable.","manual_steps":["Inventory dashboards and saved reports; identify which are genuinely viewed, and by whom","Screenshot and document definitions manually \u2014 there is no reliable export","Establish who signs off marketing reporting; in a HubSpot estate this is frequently outside marketing","Scope the target reporting build as its own workstream with its own budget","Get written acceptance that pre-cutover attribution history does not migrate","Retain a read-only HubSpot seat past cutover if historic reporting must remain accessible"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"no_hubspot_source_adapter","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"tooling","issue":"The accelerator has no HubSpot source adapter \u2014 automated extraction and IR generation are not available","gloss":"The MVP source matrix is Eloqua and SFMC. A HubSpot-source engagement gets no automated inventory, no canonical IR generation and no adapter-driven disposition. This is a delivery-capability gap, not a platform gap, and it is why the source end of this readout is interview-only.","workaround":"Scope a workshop-led assessment with an explicitly reduced fidelity claim, or fund the adapter build. Either way, set the expectation in the SOW rather than at the first status meeting. The site form scan is the one automated HubSpot capability that does exist and it should be run early, because it finds the things no tenant export shows.","manual_steps":["Set expectations in the SOW: HubSpot assessment is workshop-led, not adapter-led","Provision a scoped private-app token early \u2014 scope approval is a lead-time item","Run the site form scan for off-tenant forms","Use UI exports plus ad-hoc API scripts for the object inventory","Re-verify every verification_required entry in the HubSpot manifest before it drives a client-facing number"],"verification_required":false}]

migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml for the source end — 26 gap patterns, each carrying a severity_by_target that separates classic SFMC from Marketing Cloud Next, and this pack uses the classic half throughout. capabilities/platforms/sfmc.yaml for the target end — the real capability manifest and its four named gap patterns, two of which (loopback_flow, filter_membership_runtime) are the same constraints the HubSpot manifest describes from the other side. docs/specs/tier-2/sfmc-target-adapter.md for what the accelerator actually does at the target: scaffolds, documents DE requirements, and leaves Contact Builder and send infrastructure to the operator — which is what the sfmc_classic_readiness supplement set asks about.
